output.summary: formatPrice gains a required currency parameter and tax gains an optional rate parameter, with callers updated to match. A config currency value also changes from USD to EUR, and legacyLabel changes its label text. Check that the config change is intended given callers hardcode 'USD'.

groups.title: formatPrice gains a currency parameter
groups.description: formatPrice now requires a currency and prefixes it to the output. Read first; confirm every caller supplies a currency.

groups.title: Callers pass 'USD'
groups.description: Checkout, invoice, receipt and the aliased caller now pass 'USD'. Check that USD is right for each, especially since config.json now says EUR. viaMethod calls a different Fmt.formatPrice and only changes its argument.

groups.title: tax gains an optional rate
groups.description: tax takes a rate defaulting to 0.1, so existing behavior is preserved for old calls. Check the default matches the previous constant.

groups.title: Callers pass a 0.2 rate
groups.description: order_total and refund now pass 0.2, which changes their results from the 0.1 default. Confirm the rate change is intended. use_calc only changes an argument on an unrelated Calc.tax method.

groups.title: Config currency and legacy label
groups.description: The config currency changes to EUR and legacyLabel's text changes; these look unrelated to the signature changes. Check whether the EUR change conflicts with the hardcoded 'USD' callers.

edgeVerdicts.reason: checkout.ts imports formatPrice from ./price.ts and calls it.
invoice.ts imports formatPrice from ./price.ts and calls it.

viaAlias.ts calls fmt, which reexport.ts re-exports as an alias of formatPrice from ./price.ts.
f is a Fmt and calls the unrelated Fmt.formatPrice method defined in fmt.ts, not price.ts's function.
Calc().tax calls the Calc.tax method in calc.py, not the module-level tax in tax.py.
orders.py imports tax from tax and calls it.
refunds.py imports the tax module as t and calls t.tax.
